findings.statement: C13-CLOUDFLARE-STORAGE-LIMIT requires a write seam to refuse an over-limit payload before opening a transaction. requireStorableBlob does that for blob payloads, but requireExecutableStatement — the bound-parameter and statement-length check — runs inside execute, which is inside storage.transactionSync for a transactional write. The observable rule still holds because a throw inside transactionSync rolls back, so the durable log is unchanged, but the refusal is a rollback rather than a pre-check.
findings.modelled: LocalStoreLaws.txn_refuses_over_limit states the observable consequence (refusal with the state untouched), which both mechanisms satisfy.

findings.statement: ActorLocalStore is a transaction-scope seam (transaction, read, activateActor, and a record-set declaration blob pair), not a key/value store, and no prefix listing exists anywhere on it. The kernel-facing key/value projection that host.store.get/put/delete/list/txn describes has no implementation in either package today; every durable read and write is SQL through a transaction handle.
findings.modelled: LocalStoreLaws is the contract an adapter for this seam owes, including deterministic sorted-key iteration, which no current store offers as a seam operation.
findings.disposition: 2026-09-02, not closed. ActorLocalStore stays a transaction-scope seam and this lane did not change it. The kernel-facing key/value projection the finding names (host.store.get/put/delete/list/txn, with deterministic sorted-key iteration) is extraction-stage work: the projection is a kernel-facing surface, its shape follows from the executable kernel's store opcodes rather than from any substrate, and building it inside a Cloudflare content lane would fix that shape from the adapter end. The finding therefore stands as written, with the R2 content work recorded under SC-F3 leaving it untouched: nothing in this lane added, removed or narrowed a store-seam operation.

findings.statement: §8.2 declares get(ref, range?) and stat(ref). The R2 object repository implements neither: it offers whole-object put and get with digest verification and a 32 MiB buffered bound, and no class in packages/agent-core-cloudflare extends ContentStore. Range and stat exist only on the memory and sqlite stores, where a range is a slice of an already-buffered object. C13-CONTENT-RESOLUTION is verified against the sqlite store, so no verified row covers R2 content resolution.
findings.modelled: ContentLaws models head and range as first-class operations, with range_refuses_outside matching ByteRange.read's refusal rather than R2's clamping.
findings.disposition: 2026-09-02, closed in code and in the contract suite; one row placement and one live-evidence gap remain and are stated rather than papered over. R2ContentStore (packages/agent-core-cloudflare/src/content-object.ts#R2ContentStore) is the first class in that package to extend ContentStore, bound to one TenantId per SPEC §8.4 rule 1, with put/get(ref, range?)/stat(ref) over R2ContentObjectRepository#head and #readRange: stat is R2's own head, and a window is R2's ranged get rather than a slice of a buffered whole. The refusal the model asked for is now the seam's: ByteRange.resolve(size) (packages/agent-core/src/content/range.ts) hands a substrate the window as data, so the range is resolved against the size head reported before any body is requested, and read() is expressed through the same call so one rule serves every substrate. That refusal is load-bearing rather than decorative, measured against the platform in cloudflare/test/cloudflare/content-store.test.ts: R2 clamps an over-long window silently (offset 4 length 10 of six bytes answers two bytes while reporting size 6) and refuses an offset past the object and a zero-length window at its end with an opaque 'not satisfiable (10039)' error carrying no code from this taxonomy. The seam answers content.invalid-range for both out-of-bounds windows and an empty Uint8Array for the empty one, never asking R2 for either. Failure taxonomy is definitive throughout: content.not-found for an unresolved ref, content.invalid-range from the core range rule, operation.invalid-input for a bad digest, tenant, hint or an over-bound read, operation.invalid-output for a platform size that is not a safe integer or a body length that is not the window requested, codec.invalid for metadata, checksum, media type or whole-body digest disagreement, protocol.invalid-state for a failed R2 call. The 32 MiB buffering bound now applies to what enters the isolate: an object past it is still refused on a whole read against R2's reported size before the body is fetched, a window is bounded by the window, and stat answers for an object the reads refuse because it buffers nothing. What a proper window can be checked against is stated, not overclaimed: the address is a digest of the whole object, so a window rests on the object metadata and on the SHA-256 R2 itself holds (the workerd test asserts R2 reports that digest and refuses a write whose body disagrees with it), while a window covering the whole object is digested and compared to the address. The contract suite is one parameterised body, cloudflare/test/content-store-contract.ts, carrying the core suite's five claims in the core suite's order and titles; it runs against R2 and the Durable Object SQLite store in the structural runtime and against R2 on workerd. It restates rather than imports test/content/contract.ts because a cross-package import would mix source-built and package-built AgentCoreError, ByteRange and ContentStore classes and make every code and instanceof assertion vacuous. Two things stay open. (1) No conformance row can name this evidence under C13-CONTENT-RESOLUTION: that atom is W1-owned, one row exists per atom repo-wide, a fragment may hold only rows whose owner matches the SPEC-declared owner, and ledger.mjs refuses a row citing tests owned by another wave, so the W1 row in foundation.json cannot cite cloudflare/test/**. The evidence is recorded on the W8 row that can hold it, C13-CLOUDFLARE-STORAGE-LIMIT, whose bounds now state what the R2 content path does and does not claim, and the resolution tests carry the C13-CONTENT-RESOLUTION label so the atom they answer is visible. Moving the atom or inventing a Cloudflare one is a W0/SPEC decision, not this lane's. (2) The workerd evidence is miniflare's local R2, not the deployed service; no live scenario was added, because the archived live run fingerprints test/live/phase-1..4.test.ts and adding a scenario without a re-run would either stale that archive or fabricate evidence. The owed live scenario is named in C13-CLOUDFLARE-STORAGE-LIMIT#bounds instead.

findings.statement: The first Lean draft made an undecodable body produce no host call at all. Both §10.4 and the adapter retry it — acknowledging destroys the message, and leaving it undispositioned loses the decision — so Disposition.hostCall now retries and only acceptance acknowledges. The cross-check against the adapter is what caught it.

C13-CLOUDFLARE-DYNAMIC-STORE-LIFECYCLE (stopping preserves a domain's store, destroying releases it, and a withdrawal destroys rather than stops) is not expressible in the pinned kernel opcode set of load and call. Those verbs live on DurableObjectFacetHost as open/suspend/retire, and the row itself records that no withdrawal path calls retire yet.

findings.statement: AGENTS.md requires promise pipelining wherever possible and requires stub disposal, and no conformance atom observes either property. Nothing in the repository establishes that a call on a promise stub answers as a call on its resolution, and nothing observes a callee-side release on disposal.

findings.statement: ClaimedAlarmStorage.getAlarm reports an owner's claim only while the physical alarm is non-null, so a claim table with a torn-down physical alarm reads as unarmed rather than as armed-but-unsynchronized. The Lean model keeps arbitration over the claim table and models get as the physical slot, which is why the two agree: the claim table is the repair source in both.

Four of the six law sets have no satisfiability witness yet, so a theorem resting on one of them could in principle be vacuous. AlarmLaws and ContentLaws are witnessed in formal/AgentCore/Substrate/Witness.lean; the other four record the exact proof each still needs rather than closing with a degenerate witness whose interesting laws would be vacuous.
